subject: Acme Health: on-prem demarcation & egress readout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz@acmehealth.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@equinnix-colo.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme Health: on-prem demarcation & egress readout

Hi Liz / Carlos —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per request, I’m attaching the first-pass demarcation diagram for the private deployment at Acme Health and a short runbook excerpt showing the egress proofing steps we discussed. High-level notes: 

- Control plane (managed by Redwood): lives in a customer-dedicated tenant inside your VPC with a narrow set of control-plane endpoints exposed via a customer-managed ALB. We are proposing mTLS with client-auth for the control-plane APIs.
- Data plane (customer-owned): inference workers run in your colo/subnets; we recommend a private NAT and a dedicated egress IP block for telemetry and model updates.
- Egress policy: outbound only to the approved Redwood artifact and telemetry endpoints; DNS egress is resolved via a customer-managed forwarder to preserve internal auditing.

Attachments: 2028-05-16_acme-demarcation-diagram_v1.pdf (diagram), runbook excerpt.

Primary asks from us: 
1) Confirm that the colo environment supports static, routable egress IPs and that the security team is OK with the proposed ALB in front of control-plane endpoints.
2) Any constraints on accepting inbound control-plane connections from Redwood-managed CIDR blocks (we can also support a customer-initiated reverse tunnel if preferred).

I’ll follow up with an updated egress matrix and a small worksheet for the network team. Looking to schedule a short ops readout next week to lock down cutover windows.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Liz Harper <liz@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@equinnix-colo.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health: on-prem demarcation & egress readout

Karthik —

Appreciate the diagram. A few quick clarifications from our infra/security side: 

- Static egress IPs: we can allocate a small pool but it must be NATed through our edge firewall. Is Redwood ok if that IP block is shared across a set of customer hosts or do you need a one-to-one mapping per worker?
- ALB placement: we typically require a private ALB inside a management subnet (no public IPs). Is the proposal here for an internal ALB or an internet-facing ALB with security group restrictions?
- Reverse tunnel: if you can support an outbound-only model from our side (reverse tunnel from control-plane to Redwood), that reduces our inbound surface; curious about the trade-offs.

We’re looping in our colo contact (Carlos) to confirm local routing capabilities. Can your team prepare a brief comparison (1-page) of inbound control-plane vs reverse-tunnel approaches so our security reviewers can make a call?

Thanks,
Liz
Liz Harper
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Health
liz@acmehealth.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@equinnix-colo.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-17T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health: on-prem demarcation & egress readout

Liz —

Quick answers and an ask from our side.

1) Egress IPs: Redwood prefers a small, stable set of routable egress IPs per deployment (we use that for model pull ACLs and telemetry allowlists). However, we can operate with a shared NAT as long as you provide the static NAT IPs and a mapping table. One-to-one is not required.

2) ALB placement: we recommended an internal (private) ALB in the management subnet — no public IP. The diagram labels were ambiguous; proposal updated in the attached egress matrix spreadsheet (2028-05-17_controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx).

3) Reverse tunnel vs inbound: brief summary below (I’ll also attach a 1-pager):
   - Inbound control-plane (our APIs exposed to your ALB): simpler operationally for Redwood, lower latency for ephemeral control signals, but requires you to permit inbound from our control-plane CIDR.
   - Reverse tunnel (customer -> Redwood outbound connection): reduces inbound surface for you, we must maintain a long-lived outbound connection and a small relay fleet; slightly higher operational complexity and a small additional egress bandwidth cost on your side.

Ask: can Carlos confirm whether the colo firewall team requires NAT and whether they can host the internal ALB in a management subnet with route to the worker subnets? If so, we’ll produce the two short comparison docs by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Product Security Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachment: 2028-05-17_controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Harper <liz@acmehealth.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@equinnix-colo.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-18T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme Health: on-prem demarcation & egress readout

Thanks all — short readout and next steps.

- Carlos: if the colo can host an internal ALB and provide the static NAT block (even a small /29), that maps neatly to our preferred flow (internal ALB + static egress). If you can confirm by EOD Tues we’ll lock diagrams.
- Liz: we’ll post the 1-page inbound vs reverse-tunnel comparison and a trimmed runbook snippet to Confluence (link below) and update the Drive diagram to include the management-subnet label clarified.
- Action items (owners):
   * Carlos (Equinix contact) — confirm ALB placement and NAT capabilities (due 2028-05-21)
   * Kimberly (Redwood) — publish the 1-pager & runbook snippet to Confluence (due 2028-05-18) — done (attached runbook-snippet).
   * Karthik (Redwood) — schedule the ops readout (30m) for the week of May 22, invite firewall & network owners.

We’ll keep the control-plane CIDR locked to 10.240.0.0/22 for now in the docs and can move to customer-provided SKUs if needed during provisioning.

Confirmed attachments posted: 2028-05-16_acme-demarcation-diagram_v1.pdf, 2028-05-17_controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx, 2028-05-18_runbook-snippet.md

Best —
Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
